title: The Tougaloo dentist and Sammy Edwards' toothache
summary: A white dentist pulls drummer Sammy Edwards' tooth on his porch so no white patient will see a Black man in his chair.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And another thing, he would watch everything, and in the south--he would say a lot of things, but this wasn't anything malicious, but he had--I just wish I had the picture because it's just so comical to think how this race issue was so simple. I believe it was Tougaloo, Mississippi that we were playing, and Sammy Edwards, the drummer, very nice drummer, he didn't go on to be sensational but he was among one of the best drummers I had and we had--
Side A of Tape 4 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Side B.)
(Side B of Tape 4 begins at this point.)

I believe it was Tougaloo, Mississippi that we played one night and Sammy Edwards, our drummer, had a terrible toothache, you could just see the misery he was in, so when I got off--we were playing a black dance--I said about a dentist. So they said we don't have a colored dentist here and two or three of them talked and talked and finally they decided well perhaps doctor so and so, a white dentist, he's pretty nice, maybe we can get him to pull his tooth tomorrow, see what he can do for him.

So early that next morning about opening time, I picked up Sammy and Leon Wright went along with me, and I don't know, Leon looked like he was saying something, he had his camera and the people went in there and talked to the dentist and told him this young man was in misery, would he look at him and see. So finally he said, well, I can't let him suffer

like that, if he doesn't mind it, I'll just move my regular chair out on the porch and I'll pull his tooth for him and do whatever I can for him, but I can't let him sit in my chair in my office and pull his tooth because suppose some other white person comes in while he's sitting in the chair; it would ruin me.

So we thought the main thing was to get Sammy out and do what he could and he gave him some kind of prescription to take after he pulled it. So he was very nice and went on and pulled it and he had a regular house chair on the porch and a towel around Sammy and Leon took the picture.
Yeah, he asked the dentist and he said yeah, that's all right.
